classifiedFinding.title: _recomputeSchedule called from non-pull paths sets rewardBudget to a value that includes mintDebt without materialising it; transient solvency gap between recomputes

classification.assetImpact: Operational reward-claim DoS whenever dispatcher-hook health degrades between a recompute-without-pull and the next _syncBudget. Recoverable via owner topUp. Closely related to C-02.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls topUp(small) — _recomputeSchedule sets rewardBudget = balance + mintDebt - committedDebt without first calling pull().
2. Dispatcher-hook health degrades between this call and the next _syncBudget (mintDebt no longer realisable).
3. Stakers accrue against the inflated budget.
4. Next _syncBudget pulls less than projected; subsequent claims revert at _safePay.
classification.likelihood: low - depends on hook health degrading in the window between a non-pull recompute and the next user interaction.
classification.assumptions: Hook health changes between the two calls.

classifiedFinding.justification: Low / state-machine consistency. The CLAUDE.md solvency invariant ('balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt') is technically approximate when mintDebt > 0; the stronger invariant the code maintains is 'V == rewardBudget + committedDebt'. Recommendation: tighten the invariant statement in CLAUDE.md, or couple topUp / setTargetAPY / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter to _syncBudget rather than the bare _recomputeSchedule.
